course.title: AI Overview — From Foundations to Responsible Applications
course.description: A visual-first, vendor-neutral AI curriculum that preserves the attached 158-lesson, 18-module syllabus and progresses from AI literacy and traditional reasoning to machine learning, generative applications, agents, production practice, and responsible AI.
course.version_scope: Vendor-neutral foundations reviewed against official documentation available on 2026-10-15. Tool-specific APIs, model names, laws, and framework versions change; verify the live official documentation before implementation.
prerequisites: No previous AI experience is required; basic computer literacy is sufficient for the introductory modules.
Mathematics and programming become increasingly important in technical modules.
Follow the learning roadmap or choose the AI literacy, model-building, application-development, or specialist track that matches your goal.
learning_outcomes: Explain major AI concepts and distinguish AI, machine learning, deep learning, predictive AI, and generative AI.
Understand data, logic, search, common learning paradigms, neural networks, and major AI specializations.
Design introductory AI experiments and applications with baselines, task-appropriate evaluation, and reproducible records.
Assess limitations, uncertainty, privacy, fairness, security, and operational risks and plan appropriate safeguards.
Communicate results and plan advanced projects with evidence, documentation, and human oversight.

stages.title: AI literacy and foundations
stages.goal: Explain what AI is, where it is used, how approaches differ, and why outputs require checking.
stages.milestone: Complete AI or Not AI? and AI Experiment Log.

stages.title: Mathematics, traditional AI, and data
stages.goal: Represent a problem, understand numerical foundations, and prepare data with provenance and validation.
stages.milestone: Complete Logic Puzzle Solver and Explore a Dataset.

stages.title: Machine learning and reliable evaluation
stages.goal: Compare learning paradigms, train baseline models, evaluate task-specific metrics, and document uncertainty.
stages.milestone: Complete a classifier and interpret its evaluation.

stages.title: Neural networks and AI specializations
stages.goal: Understand neural-network training and choose specialist approaches for data and task needs.
stages.milestone: Complete a neural network or text/image specialization experiment.

stages.title: Generative AI, LLM applications, and agents
stages.goal: Build concept-level understanding of generation, retrieval, API integration, tools, and bounded agent workflows.
stages.milestone: Complete prompt comparison, semantic search, RAG evaluation, and agent safety tasks.

stages.title: Production and responsible AI
stages.goal: Plan deployment, monitoring, security, privacy, fairness, and accountable human oversight.

stages.title: Product development and professional readiness
stages.goal: Evaluate AI product value, compare research claims, communicate evidence, and build a responsible portfolio.
stages.milestone: Complete the AI Learning and Knowledge Platform capstone plan.

learning_roadmap.learning_note: AI literacy learners can emphasize Modules 1–2 and 16–18; model builders should spend more time on Modules 3–10; application developers should focus on Modules 12–16. Specialist topics in Module 11 and Section E are optional and should be selected by use case.
